sections.text: Introduction

We recommend a periodic inspection of the tap changer
 equipment to certain a high reliability in service according to manufacture
 instructions.
 Also, we recommend that personnel well acquainted with the equipment should
 carry out the inspection.
 The Inspection should be carried out as quickly as possible with the most care
 and tidiness.

The first draft was initiated by eng. Emad Mabrouk 
Mohamed, 
and tested by eng. Wagdy Mechaiel Barsoum at El-Minia132kv substation, accepted 
by eng Metawie Aly Hassan General director, and approved by eng. Ahmed Saied 
MPIS and QC General Director at ME zone

The maintenance of 
 the OLTC consist of 3 stages:
1) Inspection:

On the rating plate, 
 inspection once a year, is recommended. This principally concerns the 
 motor-drive mechanism and refers to a visual inspection inside the motor 
 cabinet to check that nothing is loose, the heater is functioning the 
 contactor contacts are not burned in the motor-drive mechanism a counter 
 registers every tap-changer operation. During inspection the counter is read. 
 If possible, motor and counter are tested by operating one step and than back. 
 If the OLTC has its own oil conservator, the breather and the oil level 
 indicator are checked. The inspection is carried out while the transformer is 
 in service
2) Overhaul

The contact life and 
 the frequency of operations determine the time interval between overhauls. The 
 number of operation run by the OLTC is recorded by a counter, housed in the 
 motor. Mechanism cabinet the registered number of operations should be noted 
 at every inspection and overhaul. The OLTC should normally be overhauled 
 regularly at intervals of 1/5 of the estimated contact life. Therevelant 
 information is stated on the rating-plate. Hereby, the contact wear can be 
 followed and necessary preparations can be made for replacing the contacts.
3) Contact Replacement

On the rating plate 
 of the OLTC the calculated contact life at rated load is stated the contacts 
 will withstand a very larg number of switching operations for normal power 
 transformers the number of operations of the diverter switch is approximately 
 20 per day, which means that exchange of the contacts is not normaly necessary 
 during the life of the transformer

Caution: The number 
 of operations must be in no case exceed 500,000 due to weakening spring 
 tension of the contacts.
Safety Precautions
A work permit must be issued,

Safety rope with caution marks surrounding 
 the work area is required.

items: A work permit must be issued,
Personnel carrying out the maintenance should carry the suitable safety category, should be trained and qualified or directly supervised by someone who is.

Safety rope with caution marks surrounding 
 the work area is required.

Wear your safety helmet, gloves, glasses and 
 shoes,

The high voltage CB, low voltage CB of the transformer must be isolated
 & proper earthing at the two sides is required
Use only fiberglass ladders

Be sure to ground the transformer bushing terminals with on-site grounding
 equipment and with ancillary grounding cable of a thickness specified by
 on-site regulations.
Caution marks in control room is required.

sections.text: Work to be Carried Out

Check the number of turns between tap changes by cranking
 the tap changer from a raise to a lower and back to a raise position. The
 turns must not be greater than one. If the turns are greater than one use
 the following steps:
 a) Turn the crank handle clockwise from
 position 10 to position 9 until the diverter switch operates and count
 the crank handle revolutions necessary for the red mark to appear in
 the green section in the middle of the inspection.
 b) Turn the crank handle counterclockwise
 from position 9 to position 10 until the diverter switch operates and
 count the crank handle revolutions necessary for the red mark to
 appear in green section in the middle of the inspection glass.

c)
 Note the difference between the counted
 crank handle revolutions

d) To correct any revolutions greater than
 one by divided by 2 and turning the crank in the direction of the most
 turns after uncoupling the drive shaft.

e) Re-couple the motor drive at vertical part
 of the driving shaft Figure 1.

f) Repeat steps I and 2 to verify the same
 number of turns in each direction

sections.text: The Disc Brake

Wipe the 
brake disc free from grease.

Check that 
the cam disc on the "one-turn" shaft iose not affect the driving roller in the 
maintaining contact after an operation. The moving energy in the motor and the 
toothed wheels should be absorbed by the brake, and the motor-drive mechanism 
should stop with the red mark 25º from the centre of the brake pads. This can 
be adjusted by tightening both of the spring bolts on the brake.

Using the 
hand-crank, operate the motor-drive mechanism until the bake is fully open. At 
this point the length of the springs must not be less than 35 mm. If the brake 
still dose not function, oil or grease has entered the brake linings, which will 
then need cleaning.

sections.text: Clean as follows:

Using a 
pair of tongs, remove the roll pins that hold the supporting shafts on the brake 
blocks.

Then remove 
the shaft and the brake blocks.

Clean the 
brake linings on the two brake with degreasing agent.

When 
refitting the brake. Check that the brake disc is completely free from grease.

Adjust the 
spring force of the brake until the motor-drive mechanism stops within the 
tolerances given above.

Check that 
the brake for the maintaining contact prevents the arm system on the maintaining 
contact shaft from swinging beyond its normal position when the roller on the 
driving arm moves free from the cam disc. At the end of the operation, contacts 
for operation in the opposite driection shall not move when the arm system 
swings back to wards its normal position.

Un permitted swinging should be prevented by 
raising the braking force, i.e. tightening the spring bolt. An increasing spring 
force on the brake makes the maintaining contact arm swing back faster, and the 
brake for the maintaining contact must be adjusted.

sections.text: Lubrication

The bearing points of the brake blocks and the 
links should be sparingly lubricated with oil. (Use oil for plain ball and 
roller bearings.) The spur gears, the genevs wheel with the limit stop, the cam 
discs and the cam bar are sparingly lubricated with grease when necessary. (Us 
lithiurn grease for ball and roller bearings in low temperature (-50-+ 
80ºC)(-58-+176ºF) Other bearing points do not need lubrication

Note: Protect the brake disc and the brake linings 
against lubricarts. Wipe off excess lubricant
Operation test

Operate the 
driving mechanism first by manual operation and then electrically between the 
limit positions.

Check the 
limit stops by operating the OLTC to one of the end positions. When trying to 
operate it electrically beyond the end position, the motor should not start.

Check the 
mechanical end stop by trying to hand crank it beyond the end position. After a 
couple of turns on the hand crank it should be mechanically stopped.

Operate the 
OLTC electrically to the other end position and carry out the same test 
procedure as above

driving mechanism first by manual operation and then electrically between the 
limit positions.
Check the 
limit stops by operating the OLTC to one of the end positions. When trying to 
operate it electrically beyond the end position, the motor should not start.
Check the 
mechanical end stop by trying to hand crank it beyond the end position. After a 
couple of turns on the hand crank it should be mechanically stopped.
Operate the 
OLTC electrically to the other end position and carry out the same test 
procedure as above
Motor Drive Protections
Thermal overload protective switch for motor.
Limit switches (in both control and motor 
 circuits).
Mechanical end stops.
Interlocking contact in the control circuit to 
 prevent electrical operation during manual operation.
Interlocking contacts in raise and lower control 
 circuits to prevent operation in wrong direction of rotation (with wrong phase 
 sequence).
Motor 
 contactors are electrically interlocked.
